fatal_errors: The proposed Ti-6Al-4V polycrystal is unrelated to the target equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single-crystal alloys.
The tensile-test geometry, temperature range, strain rate, and measured properties do not reconstruct the target compression and CRSS experiments from 9 to 1373 K.
The hypothesis omits the central target phenomena: cryogenic inertial dulling, MSAD-dependent solid-solution strengthening, and high-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier pinning.
The claimed elongation, flow-stress, yield-strength, and temperature-limit values are unsupported by cited evidence.
Describing Ti-6Al-4V simply by an HCP structure is materially incomplete because conventional Ti-6Al-4V is an alpha-plus-beta alloy whose phase fractions and microstructure depend on processing.
explanation: The response is only broadly aligned with the general topic of temperature-dependent plasticity. Its thermally activated glide concept is generic and partly reasonable, and the proposed tensile experiment is testable, but it addresses a different material class, specimen state, loading mode, temperature regime, mechanism, and outcome. It supplies precise numerical predictions without evidence and does not engage with the target's composition-dependent CRSS, low-temperature phonon-drag/inertial effects, MSAD scaling, strain-rate-jump evidence, serrated flow, or Cottrell-versus-Suzuki discrimination. Consequently, it is not a supported alternative or a reconstruction of the target.
